extracted.intended_audience: government communications professionals (GCS staff; grades AIO, IO, G6, SIO)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary diagram/listing of the GCS Aspire curriculum modules for government communications professionals, showing module categories, module titles, level (fundamentals/practitioner/advanced), delivery method, and target grade/audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum maintenance / update policy
rubrics_metrics.description: This curriculum will be constantly updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that module list and details are subject to change; check the GCS site for the latest version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The curriculum is organised into categories such as: Fundamentals modules; GCS Accelerate modules; Modern media modules; External affairs modules; Internal communication modules; Strategic communication modules; Marketing courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category contains named modules (e.g., 'Campaigning excellence' under Fundamentals; 'Essential analytics – measuring organic impact' under GCS Accelerate; 'Introduction to modern media' under Modern media; etc.). Use the category to identify appropriate pathways/levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level
rubrics_metrics.description: Level: fundamentals / practitioner / advanced (as assigned to each module).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the document: 'Campaigning excellence — Level: fundamentals'; 'Introduction to modern media — Level: practitioner'; 'Online crisis response and media relations — Level: advanced'. Use Level to judge expected prior knowledge and intended depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method (delivery format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method: online / webinar (1 hour) / face-to-face (half day / 1 day / 2 half days / 3 hours) / webinar (half day) etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Campaigning excellence — Method: online'; 'Introduction to government communication — Method: face-to-face (1 day)'; 'COM-B – using behavioural science to communicate strategically — Method: webinar (1 hour)'. Use Method to determine time commitment and delivery logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade (target audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grade: explicit target job grades for modules (examples include AIO-G6, IO-G6, AIO-SIO, SIO-G6, and 'all grades').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the document: 'Introduction to government communication — Grade: all grades'; 'Rapid response – a practical workshop to FACT and countering misinformation — Level: practitioner; Grade: AIO-SIO'. Use Grade to determine suitability for attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships / external partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Some modules are delivered or developed in partnership with external organisations (explicitly noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Campaigning excellence — Method: online — In partnership with GCSI'. If partnership is stated, expect co-delivery or partner content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module titles / named modules (catalogue entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of the named modules offered (examples include: Campaigning excellence; Introduction to Parliament; COM-B – using behavioural science to communicate strategically; Introduction to government communication; Essential analytics – measuring organic impact; Social and search listening; FACT – countering misinformation in the media; Digital marketing – an introduction to the ecosystem; Digital storytelling – engaging your employees; Engaging stakeholders and influences using digital tools; Introduction to modern media; Modern media operation guide; Rapid response; Creating content – video; Online crisis response and media relations; Introduction to external affairs; Strategic partnerships training; Introduction to internal communication; Strategic communication; Practical approach to planning, insight and evaluation; Advanced strategic communication; Campaigning excellence; Citizen experience; Communicating locally; Advanced campaigning masterclass; Creative campaigns.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the curriculum catalogue entries; each entry is accompanied elsewhere by Level, Method, and Grade to guide selection. For full descriptions consult the online module pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal comms community resource
rubrics_metrics.description: The internal comms space (https://ic-space.gcs.civilservice.gov.uk/) is the place for internal communication professionals across government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated community/resource hub for internal communication professionals; use for peer support, resources and coordination outside of formal modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Booking and detailed descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Course bookings available via the GCS website (https://gcs.civilservice.gov.uk/professional-development/). For full descriptions of each module, go to https://gcs.civilservice.gov.uk/professional-development/gcs-aspire-curriculum/
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical requirement/instruction: to attend or get full syllabus information, use the GCS professional development pages and the specific curriculum page linked above.
